items.stem: You want to predict whether each customer will churn (yes/no) from data in BigQuery. Which model type fits?

options.rationale: Correct: logistic regression is a classifier for binary outcomes.
Linear regression predicts a continuous value, not a class.
Time-series models forecast values over time, not a yes/no label.
Clustering groups unlabeled data; it does not predict a known label.

items.explanation: Correct: a binary churn target calls for logistic regression.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of a misleading BigQuery ML model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Hold out an evaluation split separate from training data
options.rationale: Correct: evaluating on held-out data gives an honest estimate.

options.text: Remove features that leak the label
options.rationale: Correct: leakage inflates metrics and fails in production.

options.text: Evaluate only on the rows used for training
Judge an imbalanced classifier by accuracy alone
options.rationale: Accuracy hides poor recall on the minority class.

items.explanation: Correct: a held-out split and removing leakage both protect model honesty.

items.stem: Which statement creates and trains a model directly in BigQuery?

options.rationale: Correct: CREATE MODEL defines and trains a model from a query.
ML.EVALUATE measures a trained model; it does not create one.
ML.PREDICT scores with an existing model.
There is no TRAIN TABLE statement in BigQuery ML.

items.explanation: Correct: CREATE MODEL is the statement that trains a model in BigQuery ML.
